Machine-Verified Catalog · GrokBot v0.70.2

Every bot tool & RPC method, indexed.

How to use the CLI, how a GrokBot request works, and every bot tool (126) and API method (309). Architecture, roadmap, and decisions live on the truth page.

01

Quick start

Needs macOS and Node 20.3 or later. Sign in once with grokbot login, or keep the Grok Bot app signed in: without its own sign-in, grokbot reads the app's token on each call. From this repo, bun packages/grokbot-cli/src/cli.ts runs the same CLI from source.

# install, then check auth and list your bots
$ npm install -g grokbotagent-cli
$ grokbot whoami
$ grokbot agents

# give a bot a job and wait up to 10 minutes (flags go before or after the command)
$ grokbot ask "<task>" --agent "Primary Test" --timeout 600

# long job: dispatch now, wait on the job id later
$ job=$(grokbot send "<task>" --agent <agentId>)
$ grokbot wait "$job"

# recent transcript, or stop the current run
$ grokbot tail -n 20 --agent <agentId>
$ grokbot interrupt --agent <agentId>

ask and wait return once the Done Rule settles, delegations included. Exit 3 means a card awaits the owner (grokbot approvals); exit 4 means the wait timed out and grokbot wait <job> resumes it. For Claude Code, Hermes, Codex, or Cursor, copy skills/grokbot/SKILL.md from the installed package ($(npm root -g)/grokbotagent-cli) into the agent's skills folder. The legacy Python ./grokbot stays in the repo; the request lifecycle below describes it.

02

How a request works

  1. Read the token

    Active account's token from ~/Library/Application Support/Grok Bot/sand-secrets.json, decrypted with the Keychain item "Grok Bot Safe Storage" (Electron safeStorage v10: PBKDF2-SHA1, salt saltysalt, 1003 rounds, AES-128-CBC). Never stored.

    grokbot:37–66

  2. Send the message

    SendGrokBotUserMessage with a random messageId. The server accepts at once; the bot works in the background.

    grokbot:127–134

  3. Find the echo

    Every 2 s, read the transcript until our message appears (clientNonce = our messageId) and note its requestId.

    grokbot:145–158

  4. Wait for the reply

    Every 3 s, look for a reply with the same requestId. After a delegation the real answer comes in a later run, so this step returns too early.

    grokbot:159–168
POST https://api2.cursor.sh/aiserver.v1.GrokBotService/<Method>

authorization: Bearer <token from the GrokBot app>
origin:        https://cursor.com
content-type:  application/json

Transcript entry fields

kind: message
A turn. role is user or assistant. Bot-to-bot turns carry toAgent or fromAgent.
kind: send-message
A reply shown to the person. One run can post several.
requestId
Groups the entries of one run. Another bot's reply starts a new run.
clientNonce
Copy of the messageId we sent.
seq
Order of entries, sent as a string number.

Traps

TrapWhat happensDo this
api.cursor.com404.Use api2.cursor.sh.
Keychain GrokOAuthTokensOld Warp token; refreshing gives invalid_grant.Ignore it.
GetGrokBotSendStatusStays ACCEPTED after the reply.Watch the transcript or bot status.
Text that starts with a dashRead as a flag.Put -- before it: grokbot ask -- "-5".
401 or 403The sign-in expired.Run grokbot login, or open the GrokBot app once.
GrokBot app updateThe API isn't publicly documented, so fields can change.Run grokbot agents, then grokbot ask "ping" on a test bot.
03

Bot tools

126 tools a GrokBot bot can call while it works. They run on GrokBot's servers; the app only shows them. 35 ask you first. None of them deletes a bot.

Coding & subagents 7Credentials & payments 13Documents & canvas 5iMessage 8Media 2Meetings & calls 10Memory & skills 6Messages & email 11Other bots & team 12Plugins & MCP 12Profile & settings 8Slack & channels 8Tasks & routines 4Web 2Work on its computer 11Your Mac & phone 7

Coding & subagents

CheckSubagentFrom its name only, medium confidence

Checks on a background subagent that the bot started.

Name only. The app has a list of running subagents (id, type, title, start time) and subagent await and stop calls. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

CloudAgentFrom the app's code

Hands a coding job to a Cursor cloud agent (a background agent, with a 'bc' id) that works in a repository.

Shows as Coding

Shown as 'Coding' with the Cursor logo. Approval card: 'Allow {bot} to use a cloud agent?'. The chat shows 'Cursor agent: <title>'. The app tracks three kinds of cloud agent watch: launch, reply and watch. A cloud agent can also propose publishing an app; only the person who launched it can confirm, on cursor.com.

Asks you first
CreateAgentFrom its schema, medium confidence

Creates a new agent from a first prompt, and can set a name, model, base branch, machine type, pool, environment and repository URL. It returns the new agent's id.

Shows as Messaging

Shown as 'Messaging'. The fields match a Cursor cloud agent start. The error shape can carry a placement approval state of required or denied. Its message types sit in the same agent.v1 package as SendToAgent and GetAgentStatus, whose results carry bc ids, which fits a cloud worker agent better than a Bot. The app does not say outright which one it is. Not the same as creating a GrokBot bot: on 13 Oct 2026 the manager created the bot Test-Dev-1 on request, but which tool it used was not observed.

Asks you first
MessageSubagentFrom its name only, medium confidence

Sends a message to a running background subagent.

Name only. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

RequestScmConnectFrom its schema

Asks the owner to connect GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps (optionally a named repository) so cloud agents can reach the repositories.

Matched to the connect-source-control request, which ends as approved, rejected or failed. The app text is 'Connect a source control integration so cloud agents can access your repositories'. Behind a source control connect card flag. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

Asks you first
StopSubagentFrom its name only, medium confidence

Stops a running background subagent.

Name only. The app has a cancel-subagent action that takes a subagent id. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

TaskFrom its schema, medium confidence

Starts a subagent (a helper agent) with a prompt, in the foreground or background. Subagent types include explore, shell, browser use, computer use, media review, watch video, debug and custom.

Shows as Working

Seen only in the status-label function. Shown as 'On its computer' when the target is computer use, otherwise 'Working'. Approval card: 'Allow {bot} to run a background task?'. Args: description, prompt, subagent type, model, resume, attachments, mode, environment, machine. The label becomes 'On its computer' when the target is computer use.

Asks you firstStatus only

iMessage

ChatItemsFrom the app's code, medium confidence

Reads the most recent messages in one Messages conversation, with a limit (default 50, maximum 200) and a 'before' cursor to page back. Items include replies, tapbacks, attachments, edits and group events.

Needs the owner to allow Messages once (a card, then a macOS permission). After that, reads run without a card for each call. Matched by elimination: the app has 8 Messages operations (find-chats, items, search, activity, send, check-permissions, fetch-attachment, find-contacts), and this is the only name left for 'items'. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

Asks you first

Checks which macOS permissions the Messages tools have on the owner's Mac: Full Disk Access, Automation for Messages and Contacts. It also reports the tool version.

Needs the owner to allow Messages once (a card, then a macOS permission). After that, reads run without a card for each call. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

Asks you first

SendIMessageFrom the app's code

Sends a text from the owner's Messages app on their Mac, to a phone number, an email or an existing chat, as iMessage, SMS or auto. The result says whether the send was verified.

Shows as Messaging

Shown as 'Messaging'. The owner gets an approval card for each text. Always allow is offered for one-to-one messages, and 'Later messages to <recipient> from this computer won't ask'. SendToAgentFrom its schema

Sends a message to another bot, with the target agent id, a delivery mode, a title and an optional model. It returns the worker's bc id and how the message was delivered.

Shows as Messaging <bot name>

Seen in a live test: the manager bot's live activity showed tool:SendToAgent. Shown as 'Messaging <bot name>' with that bot's icon, or 'Messaging another assistant' when the name is unknown. Its message types sit in the agent.v1 package with GetAgentStatus, which reports each worker's bc id, lifecycle, turn state and pull request link. The app's delivery outcomes include delivered, duplicate, target not found, forbidden and computer unreachable. No approval surface for bot-to-bot messages was found.

SetPrimaryBotFrom the app's code

Makes a chosen bot the owner's primary (main) bot, the main point of contact that coordinates the other bots. It refuses Team Bots and channels.

The app text says a primary Bot checks in proactively and coordinates work with other Bots. Refusals: 'A Team Bot can't be your main Bot.' and 'A channel cannot be the main bot.', plus not found and invalid id. No approval card found. No dedicated status label; the app falls back to the generic 'Working' label.

Shows as Messaging <bot name>

Shown as 'Messaging <bot name>' (verb messaging, where SendToAgent uses sending). No schema found.

WakeParentFrom its name only, low confidence

Plugins & MCP

AddMcpServerFrom the app's code, medium confidence

Adds a custom MCP server (an outside tool server) to the bot's setup.

Shows as Connecting to <service>

The bot's setup prompt says never to call it from memory, skill or routine text without first asking the owner in a question widget. The app lets owners add a custom MCP server for everyone using a Bot. Label is 'Connecting to <service>', or 'Connecting to a third party app' when no service is named.

Asks you first
AuthenticateMcpServerFrom the app's code

Starts the sign-in or allow step for an installed MCP server or plugin connector, so the owner sees a connect card and can allow it.

Shows as Connecting to <service>

The app tells the bot to call it when an installed MCP server has no callable tools because it is not allowed yet. The result is success, or rejected with a reason. Label is 'Connecting to <service>', or 'Connecting to a third party app' when no service is named.

Asks you first
GetMcpServerStatusFrom its schema, medium confidence

04

API methods

309 methods on aiserver.v1.GrokBotService. 62 were tested live on the owner's account, 116 are explained from the app's code, the others from their schema.

Bots and conversations 68Actions inside a chat 39Integrations, credentials and payments 88Cloud computer 42Staff only 72
Bots and conversations68

Create and manage bots, send messages, read transcripts, tasks, routines and settings.

Transcript

CommitGrokBotTranscriptEntriesTested, returned an error

The bot runtime's own transcript writer: saves and deletes transcript rows in one batch, with a conflict check per row. The server only accepts it from bots on the older box harness, so it cannot delete messages for current bots.

Send agentId, generation, entries (rows to write), deletes (rows to remove), sessionId · Get committedCount, deletedCount, rejections (per row: seq and currentUpdatedSeq)

Tested 13 Oct 2026 on Test-Dev-1 (harness temporal) with two rows to delete: refused with failed_precondition 'Transcript writer fenced: The box writer may not commit transcript rows for an agent whose harness is TEMPORAL.' (not retryable). Nothing was deleted. All current bots use the temporal harness. There is no user-facing method to delete one message.

Destructive
ListGrokBotTranscriptEntriesTested live

Returns a page of a bot's transcript rows (message, send-message, user-attachment, event), the latest rows by default, with beforeSeq paging further back. The desktop app uses it to load the end of a conversation, and the CLI tail command uses the same call.

Send agentId, limit, sessionId (empty string for the main conversation), optional beforeSeq, optional generation, optional unreadBoundaryMs · Get entries (seq, entryKind, body as base64 JSON, updatedSeq, entryId, or blobHash when the body is stored as a blob), generation, cloudAgentPeerIds, unreadAnchor

Probe with agentId and limit 5 returned 5 rows (kinds send-message and message). The app asks for limit+1 rows to learn whether older rows exist. Large bodies come back without body and with blobHash, and the app fetches them through PresignSandBoxStoreReads (same service, documented in the sandbox group) with relPaths of blobs/<blobHash>. int64 fields such as seq are JSON strings. A reply row shares the requestId of your echoed message. Checked 14 Oct 2026 (Phase 01 build): the response held only entries; generation is omitted when it is 0 (proto3 JSON drops zero values), so treat a missing generation as "0". Checked live 14 Oct 2026 (Phase 01 delegation run): in decoded bodies, toAgent on an assistant message and fromAgent on a user message are objects, not strings: toAgent {id, name, kind} and fromAgent {id, name}, where id is the other bot's agentId. The delegate's reply lands in the sender's chat as a user message carrying fromAgent and its own clientNonce. Every row of one bot run shares a requestId (our echo, the bot's notes, its toAgent row); the delegate's fromAgent row starts a new run with a new requestId that the bot's final reply shares (rows #115 to #120). updatedSeq equalled seq on all observed rows. Checked live 15 Oct 2026 (widget turns): a card closes through body-level fields on a new version of the card row (respondedValue, widgetDismissed, widgetSkipped; secretProvided for secret cards), not through message.status. After the owner resolves a card, the bot replies in a NEW run (new requestId); nothing links it explicitly except the server turn number in entryId (t51s0 card, t51s1 reply). Seq numbers can skip (143, 148 never returned).

Read-onlyUsed by CLI
WatchGrokBotTranscriptsTested live

Opens a long-lived server stream that pushes live changes for the account's bots: new, changed or deleted transcript rows, conversation clears, run state and roster changes. The desktop app uses it instead of polling to keep every conversation current.

Send cursors (one per bot: agentId, generation, afterUpdatedSeq, sessionId), includeUnlistedAgents (the app sends true), inlineBodyMaxBytes · Get A stream of frames. Frame types: connected (streamId), rows (entries, deletes, replay flag), cleared (newGeneration), cursorTooOld, heartbeat, agentState (live and client state per bot), computerActions, agentStateChanged, turnFailed, rosterChanged, boxState, pageTitleChanged

Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: connect protocol over HTTP/1.1 works (content-type application/connect+json, connect-protocol-version 1, each frame = 1 flag byte + 4-byte big-endian length + JSON). Frames seen: connected (streamId, serverTimeMs, absoluteLifetimeMs 1195000, so about 20 minutes per stream), agentState (the first has snapshot true and covers every bot on the account, even with one cursor), boxState, rows (agentId, entries with seq, updatedSeq, entryId, entryKind, base64 body), heartbeat every 10 s. A send showed live isRunning, then isComposingMessage, then idle, plus the new rows, within about 4 s. Rows carry the agentId at frame level, not per entry. Start the cursor at the bot's highest updatedSeq to skip the replay. Checked 14 Oct 2026 (Phase 01 build): each decoded frame is a JSON object keyed by its type, for example {"agentState": {...}} or {"connected": {...}}, not an object with a type field. A cursor without generation (or with "0") connects fine.

Read-onlyStream

Bot status & sessions

SetGrokBotAgentClientStateTested live

Stores per-user, per-bot interface state on the server: mark a bot read or unread, hide it from the sidebar, and turn update notifications on or off. The app calls it when you read, mark, hide or mute a bot.

Send agentId plus any of markRead, markUnread, hiddenFromSidebar, notifyOnUpdatesEnabled (also notificationsEnabled in the schema) · Get state (unreadCount, lastViewedAtMs, lastActivityAtMs, lastEntryId, lastEntryKind, lastMessagePreview, notificationsEnabled, notifyOnUpdatesEnabled, hiddenFromSidebar, updatedAtMs)

Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on the test bots: markRead set unreadCount 0, markUnread set it to 1, notifyOnUpdatesEnabled false then true toggled it (false is left out of the reply). The same state comes back in ListGrokBotAgentStatuses and in the stream's agentState frames.

Writes
ListGrokBotAgentStatusesTested live

Returns, for each bot you list, the live run state and your own client state. It tells you whether a bot is running a turn right now, which tool it is using, and the unread count.

Send agentIds (list of bot UUIDs) · Get statuses: per bot, agentId, isRunning, live (isRunning, isComposingMessage, isRetrying, activity {kind, tool, detail, target, callId}, awaiting, updatedAtMs, staleAfterMs, sessionId, hasRunningSubagents, surfaceTaskId) and client (unreadCount, lastViewedAtMs, lastActivityAtMs, last entry and message previews, notification flags, hiddenFromSidebar)

Confirmed in live tests: isRunning and live.activity (tool name) tracked a delegation test correctly. The desktop app does not call it, it receives the same live and client objects in agentState frames from WatchGrokBotTranscripts. In an idle probe the live object held only agentId, updatedAtMs and staleAfterMs, so false and zero values are left out of the JSON and a missing isRunning means false.

Read-only
ListGrokBotAgentSessionsFrom the app's code

Lists the sessions a bot has, each with an id and a kind (main, direct message, group, Slack DM or thread, or Teams DM, thread or group chat). The app uses it to list a bot's sessions.

Send agentId · Get sessions (sessionId, kind, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, lastActivityAtMs)

Probe on the owner's bot returned an empty object (no sessions listed). The default conversation is addressed with sessionId empty string in the other calls. Kinds come from the app's enum: MAIN, SLACK_DM, SLACK_THREAD, DM, GROUP, TEAMS_DM, TEAMS_THREAD, TEAMS_GROUP_CHAT.

Read-only

Attachments

ReadGrokBotAgentAttachmentChunkFrom the app's code

Reads a byte range of a bot's stored file (an attachment or asset) through the server. It is the server route of three the app uses for attachments (store, gateway, server), used when the sand_attachments_via_server flag is on, or in group chats when the grok_bot_group_chats flag is on.

Send path (absolute path under <data root>/agents/<agentId>/attachments or .../assets), offset, length, optional sessionId · Get data (bytes), totalSize

Not probed because it needs a real path. The app asks for at most 4 MB per call and checks the returned byte count against totalSize. NotFound is treated as a missing file. The app refuses to call it for paths outside the attachments and assets folders.

Read-only
ResolveGrokBotAttachmentReadsFrom the app's code

Turns attachment paths into short-lived download links. The app resolves a batch of paths for a bot, then downloads each file with HTTP range requests.

Send agentId, paths (attachment paths), optional sessionId · Get reads: per path, outcome (STORE, NOT_IN_STORE, NO_STORAGE), url, expiresAtMs, contentType, sizeBytes, etag

Not probed. When a link answers HTTP 403 the app resolves again to get a fresh link. If the server answers Unimplemented the app treats the feature as unavailable.

Read-only
UploadGrokBotAgentAttachmentChunkFrom its schema, low confidence

By its fields it uploads one chunk of a file to a bot (uploadId, fileName, offset, totalSize, data, optional sha256). It is superseded in current app code: the app uses BeginGrokBotAttachmentUpload and a presigned PUT instead.

Send agentId, uploadId, fileName, offset, totalSize, data (bytes), optional sha256Hex, optional sessionId · Get receivedBytes, optional path

No call site in the app bundle. Not probed. The chunk behavior is read from the field names only.

Writes
BeginGrokBotAttachmentUploadFrom the app's code

Starts an attachment upload for a bot and tells the app how to send the bytes: one PUT, a multipart upload, use the bot's box, or refuse. The app calls it first whenever it uploads a file to the server store.

Send agentId, fileName, sizeBytes, optional sessionId, supportsStoreAttachmentRefs and supportsMultipart (the app sends true for both), optional sha256Hex (sent for small files) · Get mode (USE_BOX, SINGLE_PUT, MULTIPART, REFUSED), uploadToken, sessionExpiresAtMs, put (url, headers, expiresAtMs) for a single PUT, partSizeBytes and partCount for multipart, refusal, limitBytes, useBoxReason

Flow: Begin, then PUT the bytes to the returned url (for multipart ask PresignGrokBotAttachmentUploadParts for part urls), then CompleteGrokBotAttachmentUpload returns an alias. AbortGrokBotAttachmentUpload cancels. Refusal values: TOO_LARGE, AGENT_FULL, EXPIRED, INCOMPLETE, SIZE_MISMATCH, NOT_AN_IMAGE, TARGET_CHANGED, UNSUPPORTED_TYPE. Not probed because it creates an upload session.

Writes
PresignGrokBotAttachmentUploadPartsFrom the app's code

For a multipart upload, asks the server for upload URLs for specific parts. The app then PUTs each part's bytes straight to its URL and asks again for a part whose URL has expired.

Send uploadToken, parts (partNumber and checksumSha256 for each part) · Get parts (partNumber, offsetBytes, sizeBytes, target {url, headers, expiresAtMs}), put, refusal

Not probed. Only used when BeginGrokBotAttachmentUpload answers MULTIPART.

Writes
CompleteGrokBotAttachmentUploadFrom the app's code

Finishes an upload after the bytes were sent and returns an alias for the stored file. The app uses that alias as the file's reference when it sends the message (inferred from the staging code).

Send uploadToken · Get alias, fileName, sizeBytes, contentType, or refusal and limitBytes

Not probed. The app treats an empty alias as an error. Refusal uses the same enum as BeginGrokBotAttachmentUpload.

Writes
AbortGrokBotAttachmentUploadFrom the app's code

Cancels an upload session. The app calls it when an upload fails or the user cancels, and it only logs any error from this call.

Send uploadToken · Get nothing (empty response)

Not probed.

Client presence

ReportGrokBotClientPresenceFrom the app's code, medium confidence

Tells the server which bot the user is looking at on this device, and optionally that they are typing to it. The desktop app sends it when the window gains focus or the viewed bot changes, sends viewing=false when the user leaves, and renews it before the lease runs out.

Send agentId, viewing (true or false), surface (the desktop app sends DESKTOP), optional trigger (TYPING), optional intent (not used by the app) · Get presenceTtlMs (how long the server keeps the presence), optional intentAction and intentReason (not read by the app)

Not probed. What the server does with presence is not visible in app code. A likely use is skipping alerts for a bot you are already viewing, but that is unconfirmed. The app backs off when it is rate limited. surface values: DESKTOP, MOBILE, GLASS.

Writes
ReportGrokBotDesktopActivityFrom the app's code, medium confidence

Tells the server whether this desktop install is currently active: signed in, not locked or idle, window alive and banners allowed. The app renews the lease about halfway through and sends active=false on shutdown.

Send installId (this Mac's machine id), active (true or false) · Get leaseMs (how long the server holds the active state)

Not probed. The app's own routesToDesktop check uses the lease, so it probably decides which device shows alerts, but the server side is unconfirmed. installId is this Mac's machine id.

Writes
ReportGrokBotNotificationPermissionFrom the app's code, medium confidence

Conversation control

SendGrokBotUserMessageFrom the app's code

Sends a user message to a bot. The server accepts and dispatches it, the app counts ACCEPTED_BOX, ACCEPTED_TEMPORAL and DUPLICATE as accepted, and the reply arrives later as transcript rows.

Send agentId, messageId (client UUID, echoed back as clientNonce), text, sentAtMs, sessionId (empty string for main); optional richText, replyToId, isFork, attachmentPaths and attachmentNames, taskId, source, sendSource, initiator, enterEpochMs, composedAtMs, traceparent, machineId, mcpConfigJson, onePasswordAppInstalled · Get dispatched, mode, workflowId, delivery (ACCEPTED_BOX, ACCEPTED_TEMPORAL, DUPLICATE, REFUSED), refusal (failureCode, message)

Confirmed in live tests: it dispatches the message and the bot replies via transcript rows. source is the client surface (DESKTOP, MOBILE, GLASS), not a content source. sendSource is CHAT, PUSH, APP_INTENT or ACTION_BUTTON_DICTATION. initiator is USER, TEMPLATE_IMPORT, TEMPLATE_SHARE, CARD_ACTION, PLUGIN_SETUP or TEACH_RECORDING. The app also counts DUPLICATE as accepted, which suggests the server de-duplicates on messageId (unconfirmed). If the call fails with Unavailable and no retry-after, the app checks GetGrokBotSendStatus and re-sends only if the result is NOT_FOUND. int64 fields are JSON strings.

The app's local debug endpoint reports a bot as live when any of its meetings is JOINING or LIVE. The repeat field describes a schedule (frequency, interval, daysOfWeek, time, timezone).

Sensitive
ResolveGrokBotAutoReviewApprovalTested live

Answers an Auto-review approval card. The app shows one when a bot action was flagged as risky: a shell command (on the host computer or in the bot's box), an MCP tool call, a phone call, a meeting join, or another sensitive action. You approve, deny, or always allow.

Send agentId, requestId (message.approval.requestId; no entryId), resolution (GROK_BOT_AUTO_REVIEW_APPROVAL_RESOLUTION_APPROVED, _DENIED or _ALWAYS), approvalPlatform ('desktop'), approvedCommand (optional), sessionId (optional), meetingJoin (for meeting joins). · Get dispatched (whether the answer was handed on), workflowId (optional).

Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on Staff Test with the account's allow rule removed for the test (restored after). The card is a send-message row with message.type auto-review-approval and message.approval {requestId, status pending, surface (box_shell), summary, summaryCopy, reason, command, proposedRule}; while it waits, ListGrokBotAgentStatuses shows live.awaiting {tabId 'auto-review', reason}. Body: agentId, requestId (from approval.requestId, no entryId), resolution GROK_BOT_AUTO_REVIEW_APPROVAL_RESOLUTION_DENIED / _APPROVED / _ALWAYS, approvalPlatform 'desktop'. Each returned dispatched true with a workflowId. DENIED: card status denied, the command did not run, the bot reported it. APPROVED: card status approved, the command ran. ALWAYS: card status always and the command ran, but nothing was added to autoReviewInstructions and the same command was flagged again next time. Answering a card twice gives 404. Short forms like 'denied' give 400. Auto-review is not consistent: the same 'sudo rm -rf' on a missing folder was flagged once and passed once; 'curl ... | sudo bash' was flagged every time.

Sensitive
ResolveGrokBotLocalToolPermissionTested live

Answers a permission card for a local tool, which is a tool the bot wants to run on one of your own devices. You can allow once, deny, always allow, or never allow.

Send agentId, entryId (the card), requestId (message.ask.requestId), resolution as a number (1 allow once, 2 deny, 3 always), sessionId (optional). · Get dispatched (whether the answer was handed on), workflowId (optional), refusal (failureCode and message) when refused.

Tested live 14 Oct 2026 on Staff Test with Execution on Local Computer set to 'Ask every time' (localToolPermission 'ask' in ~/.grokbot/settings.json; restored to 'always' after). The card is a send-message row with message.type local-tool-permission and message.ask {requestId (64 hex chars), action 'run-command', target (the command), machineId, status pending}; live.awaiting shows 'Permission needed on your computer: ...'. resolution only works as a number: 1 = allow once (status allowed), 2 = deny (status denied), 3 = always (status always); 0 and every string tried give 400. Deny works: the command does not run. Allow once and always only change the card: the Mac still refused with 'Command failed to spawn: That action was not approved on the user's computer'. The same happened when the owner clicked Allow once in the app, so it is a GrokBot bug, not the CLI.

Your computer

IssueGrokBotUserComputerCredentialFrom the app's code

Gives a registered computer a credential that it then uses for the watch, poll and submit calls. The desktop app asks for one for its own machineId.

Send machineId, credential (in the schema, but the app leaves it empty). · Get credential, expiresAtMs (int64, so a JSON string), serverAuthoritative.

The response holds a secret token, so never log it. A FailedPrecondition error carrying GrokBotUserComputerRemovedDetail means the computer was removed from the account, and the app then stops asking. serverAuthoritative changes how the app caches the credential for an account. Not called in the probe run.

Sensitive
WatchGrokBotUserComputerRequestsFrom the app's code

Opens a long-lived stream from a computer to the server. The computer says hello about itself, and the server sends small events so the computer knows when to poll for new work.

Send machineId, credential, hello (label, localRoot, terminalsFolder, standing, supervised, variant, serverAuthoritative, capabilities, kind). · Get A stream of events: connected (pendingRequestCount), notify (no fields), heartbeat (pendingRequestCount).

The desktop polls on connected and notify, and on a heartbeat whose pendingRequestCount is above zero. A watchdog aborts the stream if it goes quiet, and the app can abort it to send a new hello. Needs a credential from IssueGrokBotUserComputerCredential. capabilities lists messagesOp, localStandingGrants, aiToolSetup, shell and mobileLocalTools. Not called in the probe run.

SensitiveStream
PollGrokBotUserComputerRequestsFrom the app's code

Fetches the requests queued for a computer, such as run a command, upload or download a file, or call a local tool, and confirms earlier ones by id. The desktop calls it after each notify or heartbeat.

Send machineId, credential, ackIds (ids of requests already received), limit. · Get requests (id, enqueuedAtMs, frame). The frame is one of exec, upload, download, retire_approval, cancel, messages_op, local_tool or discover_ai_tool.

The app sends the acks on the next poll and keeps polling while a full page comes back. A cancel frame makes it drop that request's queued work. An Unauthenticated error makes it discard its credential. The frames can carry commands to run on the computer. Not called in the probe run.

Sensitive
SubmitGrokBotUserComputerResponsesFrom the app's code

Sends results back for requests the computer handled: command output, file chunks, errors, Messages results, and local tool results or permission-pending notices.

Send machineId, credential, frames (each has requestId plus one result kind: client, control, file with data, seq and last, fileError, messagesResult, messagesError, messagesConsentResult, messagesAccepted, localToolAccepted, localToolResult or localToolPermissionPending). · Get acceptedCount.

The frames can contain file contents and command output from your computer. The app batches them, retries, and flushes what is left when it shuts down. Not called in the probe run.

Asks the backend to rebuild the caller's Sand box, with or without keeping its data. The desktop app uses it for its recreate computer action and then follows progress with WatchSandBoxMigration.

Send preserve_data; force (the app always sends false); acknowledge_terminal_upgrade_schedule (optional, the app leaves it false unless set by its caller). · Get started (true or false), a reason when it was rejected, and an operation_id to follow the rebuild.

Not probed. Setting preserve_data to false most likely wipes the box data (inferred from the name and the WIPING migration phase). A rejection comes back as started=false with a reason, not as an error.

Destructive
ForceRecreateSandBoxFrom the app's code, medium confidence

A second rebuild call that takes no input. The app exposes it as its own forceRecreate action and reads the same result as RecreateSandBox.

Send none · Get started, reason and operation_id (same response type as RecreateSandBox).

Not probed. The app code does not show what 'force' skips compared with the normal recreate. Treat it as at least as destructive as RecreateSandBox.

Destructive
WatchSandBoxMigrationFrom the app's code

Streams progress events while the box is rebuilt or moved. Each event has a phase (BACKING_UP, CREATING, MOVING, CLEANING_UP, WIPING, DONE, FAILED), a detail text and an operation id.

Send from_offset_key (resume point, empty to start); include_finished (the app sends true). · Get A stream of events: phase, detail, at_ms, offset_key, operation_id.

Not probed (streaming). The app saves the last offset_key, restarts the stream when it stalls, and resumes from the saved key.

Reads the outbound network rules enforced on the live box: a restricted flag, allowed domains, and allowed TCP destinations (CIDR plus port). The desktop app uses it to decide whether its local egress tunnel may connect to a host and port.

Probe returned 404 not_found: 'no live Sand box pod to enforce an egress policy for', because no box was live. The app treats restricted=false as no limits, and applies domain rules to ports 80 and 443 only.
